Run the monthly report once

provisioning_report.Rd

It reads and sends mail, and nothing else. It does not write in the register and does not touch Entra: the register is read with the channel's token, the creations and each active row's log with the same calls the round makes, the tenant with the round's sweep. That is what lets it run outside the channel's path, as a job of its own.

Usage

provisioning_report(
  register_url,
  register_token,
  graph_token,
  graph_url,
  ledger_dir,
  now = Sys.time(),
  month = NULL,
  mailer = NULL,
  redirect_to = NULL,
  copy_to = NULL,
  channel_account = NULL,
  hosts = character(),
  secrets = character()
)

Arguments

register_url, register_token

The register's host and API token.

graph_token, graph_url

The Microsoft Graph access token and endpoint. Neither has a default, as in the round: an empty one is a directory that could not be read, and the record says so.

ledger_dir

The job's state directory, where the ledgers live.

now

When the run reads. The month, the day and the hour the mail says it read at all come from here.

month

A month "AAAA-MM" to cover instead of the one the clock gives, for a run by hand; NULL otherwise.

mailer

function(to, cc, subject, body) returning ok and errors, or NULL for no post.

redirect_to

One address replacing every recipient, or NULL.

copy_to

The address of IT: in copy on the referents' reports, and the recipient of the report to IT.

channel_account

The REDCap username that holds the register's token, the account the round writes with, or more than one while the token changes hands. With it, only their writes of owned_by pass a row to another referent and only their seals date a row, and what any other account wrote in the channel's fields is ignored; with NULL, the default, every row belongs to its creator, and the channel is whoever wrote its fields. The runner reads it from UBEP_CANALE_UTENTE, a list separated by commas, which it requires.

hosts, secrets

Named character vectors, server name to host and to the secret of its module. A server missing from either, or with an NA secret, is not read.

Value

A list that report_record() turns into the record, plus rapporti, one row per report due and per late report, with the mese it covers, for whoever reads a single run; server, what report_server_reads() answered for each server asked; recuperati, the late reports tried (a data frame of mese, destinatario and esito, mandato or fallito); and mesi_persi, the months still missing a report after the round.

Details

It also asks the instances, accounts only, through report_server_reads(): once the register and the directory have read whole, each server the register has rows on is asked for the people of those rows, the rows stopped on a disabled account included. A server that is not read stops nothing and is not an error: it is counted in istanze_non_lette, and the report goes on without what that server would have said.

The job runs every day, because an alarm on logs looks back two days at most and a monthly job cannot be watched by the absence of a record. Every day it reads, computes and leaves a record; from the 1st on it sends the previous month's report to whoever has not received it yet, until the month is complete. The ledger of what left (report_ledger_read()) is what tells them apart.

A day on which anything it needs could not be read sends nothing: the register, the creations, the directory, any active row's log, the month's ledger. An earlier month's ledger that does not read stops nothing: the people it could hold are told without their earlier reports. A report composed on half a reading would be wrong for somebody, and the next day tries again. Such a day also does not know who is due, so it judges the month on the reports the last whole reading found due, kept beside the ledger (report_due_read()); with none on record it says nothing is due, and the alarm on absence is the one that speaks.

On the 1st the run moves on to the month just ended. A month whose reports did not all leave is not given up: the first run that can send (read whole, the post on) sends the late reports of those months first, oldest first, each saying it is late and carrying the accesses activated in its own month (report_late_message()), and then the report of the month covered. The months checked are those from report_first_month() up to the month covered, excluded (report_lost_months()); a month with no list of the reports due kept takes the referents of today for it, and keeps them. The report to IT is not recovered, since it carries the state of today. Each late report that leaves is written in the ledger of its month. While a month is still missing a report after the round, the record carries RAPPORTO_MESE_PRECEDENTE_INCOMPLETO, and in_ritardo is true.

The real ledger is written only by a real run: the post on, nobody redirected, the month the clock gives. A run with the post off sends nothing to record. A redirected run is a field test: recorded in the real ledger, it would make the real month read as sent, and a test at the end of October would leave nothing to leave on the 1st of November. So it keeps a ledger of its own, and is idempotent as the real run is: the timer of a field test does not send everything again every day. A run with a forced month writes nothing at all. Neither of the two recovers a month lost: a late report that went to the test address would be written in the real ledger of its month, and its referent would never receive it.

The report to IT goes to copy_to, the address IT is in copy at on every outcome, under the name report_it_key(); the referents' reports go to the owner's account, with copy_to in copy.

A row goes to its owner as the month covered ended, at midnight in Rome between its last day and the next month's first, and not to its owner on the day of the run: log_owner() reads the row's log cut at that moment, so a write after it, of owned_by or of any other field of the channel, changes nothing. The month's reports leave over several days, until each referent has had theirs, and who is due must not change from one attempt to the next (decided on 2026-10-17): read on the day, a row passed on the 3rd would move from one referent's report to the other referent's between two attempts, after one of the two had left. Without channel_account, NULL, no write of owned_by is believed and every row stays with its creator.
